page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARM64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with 192.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core CPU tests, fall into the weak and average categories respectively, with single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 showing lower relative performance. Conversely, multi-core execution is highly efficient, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25% and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving average tier results. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average range, measuring 168.57 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

While the instance handles parallel processing and database operations efficiently, it exhibits limitations in large-scale machine learning tasks, with large-model LLM inference text generation and prompt processing scoring in the weak and poor categories. The combination of dedicated ARM64 cores, balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, and high-speed local NVMe storage makes this server profile qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads. It is optimized for applications such as static web serving, Redis database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose containerized workloads that benefit from local scratch storage.
